report_name: Espionage Group TGR-STA-0049 Deploys Novel RATs with HTTP/3 C2

threat_actors.name: TGR-STA-0049
threat_actors.description: A sophisticated cyberespionage group active since at least March 2023, targeting government entities in Southeast Asia, South America, and Europe. The group is known for using custom RATs like Squidoor, PerfectPioneer, and KUKURAT, and employing HTTP/3 for C2 communications to evade detection.
threat_actors.goals: The primary objective is cyberespionage, focusing on long-term intelligence collection and data exfiltration from strategic government targets.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: TGR-STA-0049 gained initial access by exploiting unpatched, internet-facing applications, particularly Microsoft Exchange servers.

attack_patterns.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor deployed various web shells, including ASPXSpy, Godzilla, Bysunue.aspx, and Suo5, on compromised servers to maintain a foothold and execute commands.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Attachment
attack_patterns.description: As a secondary infection vector, TGR-STA-0049 used targeted phishing emails with malicious decoy PDF attachments, such as one impersonating a document from Myanmar's election commission, to deliver malware.

attack_patterns.name: Hijack Execution Flow
attack_patterns.description: The PerfectPioneer RAT was executed using DLL Side-Loading as one of its deployment methods.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT RATs used HTTP/3 over the QUIC protocol for command and control communications to blend in with legitimate web traffic.

attack_patterns.name: Encrypted Channel: Asymmetric Cryptography
attack_patterns.description: The malware's C2 traffic was encrypted by default using TLS 1.3 as part of the HTTP/3 protocol, hindering network inspection.

attack_patterns.name: System Owner/User Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers executed the 'whoami' command after gaining a foothold via a web shell to identify the current user context.

attack_patterns.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers executed the 'ipconfig' command after gaining a foothold via a web shell to gather network configuration details.

attack_patterns.name: Account Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers executed the 'net user' command after gaining a foothold via a web shell to discover user accounts on the compromised system.

malware.name: PerfectPioneer RAT
malware.description: A Go-based RAT used by TGR-STA-0049 since July 2025. It uses HTTP/3 for C2 and is deployed via web shells, DLL side-loading, or decoy installers.

malware.name: KUKURAT
malware.description: A modular and more advanced successor to PerfectPioneer, deployed by TGR-STA-0049 since March 2026. It also uses HTTP/3 for C2.

malware.name: Squidoor
malware.description: An advanced backdoor previously used by TGR-STA-0049 before the current campaign.

malware.name: ASPXSpy
malware.description: A publicly known web shell deployed by TGR-STA-0049 on compromised Microsoft Exchange servers for initial access and payload delivery.

malware.name: Godzilla
malware.description: A web shell deployed by TGR-STA-0049 on compromised servers to establish a foothold.

malware.name: Bysunue.aspx
malware.description: A custom web shell deployed by TGR-STA-0049 on compromised servers.

malware.name: Suo5
malware.description: A custom web shell deployed by TGR-STA-0049 on compromised servers.

identities.name: Government organizations
identities.description: Government entities across Southeast Asia, South America, and Europe were the primary targets of the TGR-STA-0049 cyberespionage campaign.

identities.name: Union Election Commission of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar
identities.description: An official document from this government agency was impersonated in a decoy PDF used in a phishing attack by TGR-STA-0049.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: The vendor for Microsoft Exchange servers, which were a primary target for exploitation by TGR-STA-0049.

infrastructure.name: HTTP/3 C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: C2 infrastructure used by PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT RATs, which communicates over HTTP/3 (QUIC) on UDP port 443 to evade detection.

indicators.name: TGR-STA-0049 Web Shell Filenames
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: TGR-STA-0049 Web Shell Filenames
id: 11223344-5566-4778-899a-abbccddeeff0
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of web shell files with names used by the TGR-STA-0049 group, such as Bysunue.aspx and Suo5.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/custom-rats-target-southeast-asia-governments/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.persistence
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Bysunue.aspx'
      - '\Suo5'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web shell files with names known to be used by TGR-STA-0049.

indicators.name: Suspicious Child Process of Web Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Child Process of Web Server
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a7b-8c9d-e0f1a2b3c4d5
status: experimental
description: Detects web server processes (w3wp.exe, httpd.exe) spawning command-line interpreters, which may indicate web shell execution or exploitation.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/custom-rats-target-southeast-asia-governments/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects web server processes like w3wp.exe or httpd.exe spawning command-line interpreters, a common sign of web shell activity.

indicators.name: Anomalous Outbound QUIC from Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Outbound QUIC from Server
id: aabbccdd-eeff-4001-9234-567890123456
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound UDP traffic on port 443 (QUIC) from servers that are not expected to be QUIC clients, such as web or database servers. This may indicate C2 communication using HTTP/3 as seen with PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/custom-rats-target-southeast-asia-governments/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1071
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort: 443
    Protocol: 'udp'
    Initiated: true
  filter_client:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
  filter_server_procs:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\sqlservr.exe'
      - '\dns.exe'
  condition: selection and filter_server_procs and not filter_client
indicators.description: Detects non-browser QUIC traffic (UDP/443) originating from servers, which could be indicative of HTTP/3-based C2 channels.

indicators.name: Web Server Reconnaissance Commands
indicators.pattern:
title: Web Server Reconnaissance Commands
id: 98765432-10fe-4dcba-9876-543210fedcba
status: experimental
description: Detects web server processes executing common reconnaissance commands, which could indicate post-exploitation activity by groups like TGR-STA-0049.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/custom-rats-target-southeast-asia-governments/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-17
tags:
  - attack.t1033
  - attack.t1016
  - attack.t1087
  - attack.discovery
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\ipconfig.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects web server processes spawning common reconnaissance commands like whoami, ipconfig, and net user.
